display.title: Episode 121: The Forbidden Road, Chapter 2 (Pesach)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi's last show before Pesach: the Tzivos Hashem Pesach Experience, Shema with a visiting family, and how Reb Beryl's promise to give tzedakah brings a miracle.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week before Pesach 5744. Uncle Yossi announces the Tzivos Hashem Pesach Experience on the first day of Chol HaMoed, with storytelling, a mitzvah show and a boys' choir, then leads the Hakochainik march. Story time recaps how Reb Beryl's temper led him onto a forbidden street and cost him his fortune. A visiting father brings his daughter to say the Shema and thanks Uncle Yossi for his far-reaching programs. In the conclusion, the Rebbe tells Reb Beryl it is never too late for teshuvah: he must become kind-hearted and promise to give a tenth of all he has to tzedakah. Reb Beryl and his wife say Tehillim, while the officer gets drunk and the maid sweeps the signed paper into the fire. Reb Beryl calls back the melamed, apologizes and gives generously. Then a third-grade class recites Ha Lachma Anya in Yiddish, a three-year-old's upsherin is celebrated, and a young visitor from California says one of the twelve pesukim. Uncle Yossi explains that the show will be off the air on Yom Tov, but everyone should still say the Shema at six on Tuesday, and invite friends who have no Seder.
display.lesson: Give tzedakah generously, for giving brings blessing; it is never too late for teshuvah.
